 About the Report
About the Report 
TCS’ Integrated Annual Report for FY 2025-26 (FY 2026) covers the financial and non-
financial performance during the year, and provides information about its strategy, 
business outlook, governance practices, material issues, risks, and opportunities.
Reporting Period
This report covers the financial year 
April 1, 2025 to March 31, 2026. Unless 
stated otherwise, all data, performance 
metrics, and strategic disclosures relate 
to this period.
Reporting Entity
This Report covers information on the 
Indian and international operations 
of TCS Limited (Parent Company) and 
its subsidiaries which are collectively 
referred to as the ‘Company’.
Integrated Reporting
This Report goes beyond financial 
reporting to cover TCS’s non-financial 
performance, opportunities, risks and 
outcomes attributable to or associated 
with key stakeholders, which have a 
significant influence on the Company’s 
ability to create value.
Integrated Business Model
TCS’s ability to create long-term value 
is interrelated and fundamentally 
dependent on various forms of capitals 
available (inputs), their usage (value-
accretive activities), the Company’s 
impact on each of the capitals and the 
value delivered, and impact managed 
(outputs and outcomes).

Materiality
This Report focuses on information that 
is material to the Company’s business. 
It provides a concise overview of the 
Company’s performance, prospects, and 
ability to provide sustainable value for all 
its stakeholders. The legitimate interests 
of all stakeholders have been considered 
and all material information has been 
included in this Report.
Boundary
This report includes the sustainability 
performance across TCS’ global owned 
and operated locations. Disclosures 
extending to the value chain or select 
regions are specified where applicable. 
The financial boundary follows the 
consolidated Group reporting framework.
Audit and Assurance
TCS’ financial statements have been 
audited by B S R & Co. LLP , Chartered 
Accountants. Select non-financial data 
within the BRSR has been subject to 
reasonable and limited assurance by 
KPMG, an independent third-party 
assurance provider . The scope and 
conclusions of these engagements are set 
out in the respective assurance statements.
Feedback
Please share your feedback on this report 
at: investor.relations@tcs.com

Exclusions
All financial figures and metrics presented 
in this report are stated after excluding 
exceptional items. In FY 2026, the 
Company incurred certain non-recurring 
items, comprising of restructuring 
charges, provision towards a legal claim, 
and the impact of the new Labour 
Code in India. These have been treated 
as exceptional items and have been 
excluded from financial information and 
related explanations in management 
commentary and other non-statutory 
sections to provide a clearer view of 
underlying business performance, unless 
otherwise indicated in those sections. The 
Consolidated and Standalone Financial 
Statements continue to be reported 
in accordance with applicable Indian 
Accounting Standards.
A historic moment at the 2026 TCS London Marathon, as Sebastian Sawe became the first athlete 
to run a sub-two-hour marathon, in a world-record time of 1:59:30.
About TCS
Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) is the technology partner of choice for industry-
leading organisations worldwide. Since its inception in 1968, TCS has upheld the 
highest standards of innovation, engineering excellence and customer centricity.
Rooted in the heritage of the Tata 
Group, TCS is focused on creating long 
term value for its clients, its investors, 
its employees, and the community at 
large. With a highly skilled workforce 
of over 580,000 consultants spread 
across 56 countries and 194 service 
delivery centers across the world, the 
company has been recognised as a top 
employer in six continents. With the 
ability to rapidly apply and scale new 
technologies, the Company has built long 
term partnerships with its clients. Many 
of these relationships have endured into 
decades and navigated every technology 
cycle, from mainframes in the 1970s to 
Artificial Intelligence today.
TCS sponsors 14 of the world’s most 
prestigious marathons and endurance 
events, including TCS New York City 
Marathon, TCS London Marathon, 
Tata Mumbai Marathon, and TCS 
Sydney Marathon, with a focus on 
promoting health, sustainability, and 
community empowerment. 
TCS generated consolidated revenues of 
US $30 billion in the fiscal year ended 
March 31, 2026.  
For more information, visit:  
www.tcs.com
The TCS’ FY 2026 Integrated Annual 
Report reflects its aspiration and 
investments across the full AI stack from 
AI Data centre to delivering Agentic 
AI-led transformation.  The stack is 
structured across five integrated layers, 
infrastructure, tools, data, models, and 
applications, providing the essential 
building blocks required to design, deploy 
and operationalise AI securely and at 
scale. By bringing together resilient 
digital infrastructure, standardised AI 
and engineering tools, trusted data 
foundations, a mix of foundational 
and domain-specific models, and 
AI-embedded business applications, 
the AI Stack allows intelligence to 
be seamlessly integrated into core 
enterprise processes. This approach 
enables enterprises to move from 
technology readiness to insight-driven 
transformation, embedding AI 
responsibly into decision-making, 
operations, and value creation.

N Chandrasekaran

Letter from the Chairman
AI is a foundational technology that cuts 
across all industries. The advancements 
in AI are creating industry wide shifts 
towards automation and transformation. 
Your company has created a 
comprehensive AI strategy to provide full 
stack AI solutions to customers across 
industries. TCS is repositioning itself as an 
AI & Digital transformation partner.  
In fiscal 2026, TCS scaled up execution 
of the ‘Human+AI’ operating model and 
industry specific agent marketplace. Your 
company generated annualised revenues 
of US$ 2.3 billion in AI Services and  
US$ 11.5 billion in new-age services 
including Cloud, Data, Enterprise Solutions 
and Cyber Security. 
During the year, we launched HyperVault 
a secure by design AI infrastructure 
platform, in partnership with TPG and 
supported by a deep partner ecosystem. 
As global constraints on power, compute, 
and geography intensify, India is emerging 
as a strategic ‘+1’ destination for AI 
infrastructure. HyperVault positions us at 
the centre of this shift.
TCS is also focusing on acquiring and 
scaling next-gen capabilities through 
inorganic initiatives. This year your 
Company completed acquisition of two 
companies with deep expertise in AI, cloud, 
and SaaS. TCS announced the acquisition 
of Coastal Cloud, for US$ 700 million in 
December 2025, and ListEngage in October 
2025. These will boost TCS’ Salesforce 
practice and agentic AI capabilities. 
AI is now becoming the infrastructure 
of intelligence. It will influence how 
enterprises invest, organize supply chains, 
manage risk, and serve stakeholders. 
GenAI and agentic AI are entering a new 
phase of growth. AI will not just be a layer 
but will be the operating foundation. 
Customers will move from pilots to scale, 
embedding AI into core functions.
Your company is working closely with 
customers across industries in their AI 
led transformation. For a European 
airline, we modernised a mission critical 
crew management system using GenAI, 
rebuilding decades of legacy logic. For 
a leading U.S. utility, AI driven dispatch 
optimisation improved field efficiency by 
30%. For an electronics manufacturer, 
Physical AI is now improving safety 
and productivity.
As AI scales, key aspects of  trust, 
security, and data sovereignty will 
be non-negotiable. Enterprises will 
need an AI Operating System. This 
Operating System will be  a foundation 
of infrastructure, data, models, context, 
agents, and governance. Building it 
demands deep industry expertise, 
partnerships, and a clear understanding 
of enterprise context.
As we build a future ready TCS, we will 
lead with purpose, innovate responsibly, 
and uphold stakeholder’s trust in 
everything we do. This is anchored 
in the Tata value system—integrity, 
responsibility, inclusion, and respect for 
every individual.
Guided by Project Aalingana, the Tata 
Group’s vision for a greener, cleaner and 
more equitable future, sustainability 
remains integral to your company. In 
Fiscal 2026, nearly 79% of our global 
energy consumption was sourced from 
renewables, re-affirming our commitment 
to sustainable operations.
During the year, your company helped 
over 18.13 million people worldwide 
through our programmes in education, 
skills, healthcare, and the environment. 
Women, youth, and marginalised groups 
gained new opportunities. The TCS 
Literacy and Women Empowerment 
Programmes supported rural India 
helping the youth find jobs and learning 
digital skills. Your company’s employees 
volunteered 9.42 million hours, impacting 
12.96 million lives. 
I thank our customers, partners, and 
shareholders for their trust. I thank 
our associates for their commitment 
and ingenuity. 
As technology reshapes the world, our 
responsibility is clear - innovate with 
integrity, scale with trust, and grow 
with humanity. 
Warm regards,
N Chandrasekaran 
Chairman

Looking ahead, your Company 
will prioritize efforts across 
four focus areas:  
It is my privilege to present to 
you the Integrated Annual Report 
2025-26 of Tata Consultancy 
Services for the financial year 
ended March 31, 2026. 
The year 2026 began with expectations 
of steady global growth, soft inflation 
and easier financial conditions. The 
year witnessed positive developments 
including the signing of the landmark 
India-EU trade agreement and the 
interim India-US trade deal. However, 
by early March, the start of the West 
Asia crisis brought rising concerns about 
stagflation—falling output coupled with 
rising inflation.
Dear Shareholders,
We are in the midst of intensifying 
geopolitical tensions, shifts in trade and 
supply chains, and uneven economic 
growth.  Across markets, corporates are 
prioritising resilience, productivity and 
trust based decisions. 
In this backdrop, your company delivered 
a strong performance with the fiscal 2026 
consolidated revenue of ₹ 267,021 crore, 
delivering a growth of 4.6% over the 
previous year. The Operating Income was 
₹ 66,838 crore with an Operating Margin 
of 25.0%. The Net Income was ₹ 52,820 
crore, a growth of 8.8% over the previous 
year, with the Net Margin of 19.8%. Both 
the Operating Margin and Net Margin 
were the highest over the past four years. 
The cash flows from operations were 
105.9% of the net profit. 
Fiscal 2026 performance saw strong 
client metrics with healthy additions 
across every revenue band, validating 
the critical role of the company in 
clients’ transformation journey. Clients 
generating over US$ 100 million revenue 
annually rose by 2 to 66, and the US$ 50 
million revenue  band increased by 9 to 
139 clients. Your company signed several 
large deals including 5 mega deals in the 
year resulting in a strong demand. The 
total contract value exceeded US$ 40 bn. 
The Board has recommended a final 
dividend of H 31/- per share, subject 
to your approval. The total dividend is 
₹110/- per share for Fiscal 2026.
Letter from the Chairman
AI is now becoming the infrastructure 
of intelligence. It will influence how 
enterprises invest, organize supply 
chains, manage risk, and serve 
stakeholders. GenAI and agentic AI 
are entering a new phase of growth. 
AI will not just be a layer but will be 
the operating foundation.

Letter from the CEO
1
Our unique advantage combines a 
deep understanding of enterprise 
context, a proven track record in 
industry-leading execution, ability 
to reskill our workforce rapidly 
and at scale, strong ecosystem 
partnerships, and leadership in  
AI-driven services.
Over the years your company has 
put exceptional focus on client-
centricity.  We have earned the 
trust of over 670 global clients 
who worked with us for more 
than ten years, including over 
250 clients with relationships 
spanning over twenty years. Our 
unique advantage combines a 
deep understanding of enterprise 
context, a proven track record in 
industry-leading execution, the 
ability to reskill our workforce 
rapidly and at scale, strong 
ecosystem partnerships, and 
leadership in AI-driven services.
In FY 2026, global enterprises continued 
to navigate an increasingly complex 
macro-economic and geo-political 
environment. The rapid evolution of AI 
and the need to accelerate its enterprise 
Dear Shareholders,
adoption, further influenced leadership 
decision making. In this context, the role 
of trusted system integrators became 
even more vital, with clients increasingly 
choosing partners who bring strong 
enterprise and industry context and are 
willing to take end-to-end accountability 
for business outcomes and ROI. 
I am pleased to share with you that 
our clients further deepened their 
partnership with TCS to help them 
achieve their business outcomes. 
Global clients partnered with us to 
improve business resilience, optimize 
costs, transform operating models for 
agility, reduce technology debt through 
modernization and scale AI across 
the enterprise.
This translated into broad-based client 
additions across revenue bands, strong 
order book, and continued momentum 
in large deals. Clients showed greater 
willingness to commit to long-term, multi-
year, multi-million-dollar partnerships—
reflecting the trust they place in TCS to 
deliver certainty and value at scale over 
extended transformation journeys.  
130 of our top 139 clients generating over  
US$ 50 million in annual revenues, 
have chosen your company as the AI 
services partner.
We delivered complex, large-scale 
programs across geographies, including 
nation-scale outcomes in India. We scaled 
the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) 
into the world’s largest government 
e-commerce marketplace, with 
procurement exceeding ₹ 5 lakh crore. 
For instance, we upgraded State Bank of 
India’s YONO 2.0 to serve 20 crore users 
in 10 languages. We also modernised 
citizen services such as ePassports (over 1 
crore issued) and built the RBI’s new data 
management system, designed to handle 
250 TB for sharper economic analysis.
Our execution has been recognised 
globally. Newsweek ranked TCS #1 
among Technology Services enterprises in 
America’s Most Reliable Companies, and 
Fortune listed us among the World’s Most 
Admired Companies in 2026.
FY 2026 marked an inflection point for 
enterprise AI. For the first time since 
GenAI emerged in 2023, customers 
moved decisively from pilots to scaled 
deployments. AI became central to 
every conversation and every solution, 
accelerating adoption across industries.
This year has been pivotal for TCS. To 
realise the opportunities offered by AI, we 
set out a bold aspiration to become the 
world’s largest AI-led technology services 
company. Our strategy to realize this 
aspiration, is to be a full-stack AI services 
player from Infrastructure to Intelligence. 
We have identified five transformation 
pillars that will underpin this strategy. I 
am pleased to share that we made strong 
progress across all five pillars:
1) tcs
AI: We democratised AI access 
for all associates, ran the world’s 
largest hackathon with over 281,000 
participants, and institutionalised ‘AI 
Friday hackathons’ to build a continuous 
culture of learning and innovation. We also 
transformed internal operations through a 
customer-zero approach.
2) Redefining Services: We established a 
dedicated Services Transformation unit and 
launched a services re-design framework 
based on a Human + AI service autonomy 
model. We are taking AI-led, re-designed 
services proactively to existing clients 
and new prospects, enabling consistent 
deployment at enterprise scale.
3) Building a Future-Ready Talent 
Model: As AI reshapes roles and ways 
of working, we are acting ahead of the 
curve. In FY 2026, we invested 69 million 
learning hours and enabled 5.2 million 
competencies to be acquired. Over 
270,000 employees now have advanced 
AI skills-3x last year. We continue to hire 
globally for next-gen roles (cybersecurity, 
cloud, AI, data), with over 50% of 
experienced hires bringing advanced 
skills. Our Initial Learning Programme 
now integrates GenAI, giving every 
trainee access to leading platforms and 
hands-on learning.
4) Making AI Real for our clients: True 
value of AI can be realised by enterprises 
only when they are able to reimagine 
their business value chains leveraging 
AI to innovate their products, services 
and customer experiences. This requires 
them to modernise their core applications 
and data estate. We have created an AI 
acceleration playbook: Innovate with AI, 
Build with AI, Scale with AI, and deployed 
it across a significant number of customers 
to solve high-value problems in rapid 
12–16 week cycles.
5) AI ecosystem play: To strengthen  
our differentiation and competitive edge, 
we must be deeply embedded in the AI  
ecosystem and operate with both speed  
and scale. To do this, we are following a  
Build-Partner-Acquire approach. Alongside  
continued organic investment in our 
capabilities, we will deepen partnerships 
with leading AI ecosystem players, acquire  
world-class organizations, and launch new  
ventures. In FY 2026 we,
•  Expanded strategic collaborations 
with AMD, OpenAI, ABB, Honeywell, 
ServiceNow, Cisco, GitLab, 
Zscaler, Google Cloud, and others, 
accelerating innovation and staying 
ahead of evolving client needs. 
•  Acquired ListEngage and Coastal 
Cloud to deepen Salesforce 
and AI consulting, positioning 
us among the top five global 
Salesforce consultants. 
•  
Launched HyperVault, our AI 
Infrastructure business with TPG, 
with an initial plan to build 1GW 
of data centre capacity in India. 
Since launch, we have secured 
customer commitments, finalised 
land parcels, and progressed 
partnering agreements. We are 
engaging hyperscalers, semiconductor 
companies, and model providers, 
while we serve as the integration 
partner across infrastructure, 
engineering, and AI-led services.
Looking ahead, as customers scale AI, they  
are looking for partners who can build and  
manage a unified control plane across the  
full AI stack – Infrastructure to Intelligence. 
This control plane - an AI Operating  System -  
makes AI repeatable and governable  
through orchestration in an enterprise’s  
context and embeds trust mechanisms  
such as security, monitoring, evaluation,  
and auditability. Many enterprises have  
tools and models, but not the standardised  
control and context needed to run agentic  
systems safely in  day-to-day operations today.
This is where TCS is positioning itself as an 
Enterprise Intelligence Integrator, 
modernising software stacks, embedding 
AI agents into operations, and governing 
data and security at scale to deliver  
measurable outcomes.
As outlined by our Chairman, we will focus  
on four distinct progressions: Build 
industry-specific AI systems, construct India’s  
first high-density AI data centre, strengthen  
our Infrastructure to Intelligence  offering  
with 360
0 partnerships and establish secure,  
resilient,  sovereign AI infrastructure.
I thank our customers for their trust, our  
associates for their dedication and delivery  
excellence, and you—our shareholders—for  
your unwavering support. With our  
execution strength, deep context, and a  
clear AI-led strategy, we are well  
positioned to navigate uncertainty and  
compound value. We will stay focused on  
resilient growth, strong governance, and  
consistent returns.
Best regards,
K Krithivasan

The advent of generative AI marks a pivotal moment in technological history, 
creating a new frontier for enterprise innovation and value creation. 
Enterprises are moving from being 
digital-driven to becoming AI-driven. The 
leap from a digital enterprise to an AI 
enterprise is about harnessing the full 
potential of AI - not just as a tool, but as a 
strategic partner that empowers people, 
transforms processes, and redefines 
what is possible.
 An AI Enterprise,
• Uses data and context to guide 
every decision.
• Applies advanced analytics and 
reasoning to generate deeper 
insights and better decisions.
• Automates processes increasingly, 
enabling AI systems to act  
independently.
• Runs on intelligent software that can 
adapt and learn.
• Treats AI as a co-architect of choice, 
helping shape strategy and  
outcomes.
AI is not just 
another technology 
wave; it is reshaping 
how enterprises 
create, consume, 
and scale 
intelligence. 
Enterprise AI represents a once-in-
a-generation opportunity to reshape 
how work gets done, driving step-
change productivity, accelerating cost 
optimisation and enabling end-to-end 
business reimagination across industries.

data, models, platforms, applications, and real-world execution. Increasingly, clients are 
seeking a single, accountable partner who can orchestrate this entire stack with scale, 
security, and deep industry context.
For TCS, this end-to-end capability is a strategic differentiator. It enables TCS to move 
beyond isolated AI interventions to owning transformation outcomes—embedding 
intelligence into core operations and delivering sustained business value.

across its services portfolio, spanning 
applications and infrastructure 
operations, application development 
and modernization, cloud migration, 
service desk, cybersecurity, and business 
process operations.  This autonomy model 
enables TCS to consistently engage with 
clients to deliver higher levels of autonomy 
powered by AI. 
The Human + AI Service autonomy 
model defines a clear five-stage journey, 
progressing from AI-assisted human 
work to a fully agentic enterprise, where 
self-learning AI systems orchestrate entire 
value chains under human governance. 
The service autonomy model combined 
with rapidly advancing AI foundation 
model capabilities, provides TCS’ clients 
a predictable path to achieving higher 
level of autonomy. 
AI agents now drive significant parts of the 
software development lifecycle, improving 
time-to-market, productivity and quality. 
Enterprises increasingly recognise that 
maximising value from AI tool investments 
requires a contextual and structured 
AI-led engineering approach. In line with 
this, TCS deployed its AI engineering 
framework for a European client, 
integrating AI agents across the software 
lifecycle from translating unstructured 
requirements into structured specifications 
as well as executing spec-driven coding, 
testing, and deployment. TCS’ Human 
+ AI approach has accelerated software 
delivery, reducing the deployment cycle 
time by up to 40%.
In application operations, agentic workflows 
enable predictive monitoring and self-
healing systems, ensuring resilience and 
efficiency. A global enterprise partnered 
with TCS to transform application 
operations into AI-led AMS. TCS delivered 
zero disruption during peak periods 
consistently, 78% outage reduction, and 
over 95% business-flow visibility. 2,000+ 
self-heal automations ran daily, with AI 
improving major incident effectiveness and 
observability. 
to integrate AI into their day-to-day

03
With rapid technological advancements, 
enterprises face challenges in keeping 
up with AI and digital adoption in their 
context. Introducing a new technology in 
enterprises requires deep understanding 
of business and technology landscape, 
and making the new technology work in 
this context. To implement AI in enterprise 
context, there is a need to integrate AI 
and Agents into workflows, reimagine 
processes and integrate AI with enterprise 
data and systems.
AI presents a significant opportunity for 
enterprises to drive superior business 
outcomes by reimagining end-to-end  
industry value chains. This requires 
deep understanding of industry and 
enterprise context, modern technology 
stack, full stack integration capabilities, 
ecosystem partnerships and a robust 
domain specific transformation approach. 
Clients are increasingly seeking partners 
capable of bringing these capabilities 
together to deliver integrated and scalable 
transformation outcomes.
AI presents a unique opportunity to 
address long-standing technology debt 
that enterprises have often deferred due 
to cost, complexity and long duration of 
such initiatives. Through its AI-powered 
modernisation workbench, Code Plus, 
TCS is helping clients modernise their 
enterprise technology stacks with 
greater speed and certainty. Supported 
by reusable patterns and an integrated 
agent marketplace, Code Plus is 
accelerating modernisation initiatives and 
enabling enterprises to transform legacy 
environments more efficiently.
Enterprises recognise that scaling AI 
requires a strong digital foundation. TCS 
helps clients prepare their enterprise 
core for AI by modernising cloud and 
infrastructure, strengthening cybersecurity, 
upgrading enterprise systems, and building 
resilient AI-ready data platforms. This 
technology foundation is critical to deploy 
AI securely, reliably, and at scale. 
Alongside continued organic investment 
in its capabilities, TCS will deepen 
partnerships with leading AI ecosystem 
players, acquire world-class organisations, 
and launch new ventures. 
In FY 2026 the Company,
• Expanded strategic collaborations 
with AMD, OpenAI, ABB, Honeywell, 
ServiceNow, Cisco, GitLab, 
Zscaler, Google Cloud, and others, 
accelerating innovation and staying 
ahead of evolving client needs. 
• Acquired ListEngage and Coastal 
Cloud to deepen Salesforce and AI 
consulting, positioning TCS among the 
top five global Salesforce consultants. 
• Launched HyperVault, TCS’ AI 
Infrastructure business with TPG, 
with an initial plan to build 1GW of 
data centre capacity in India. Since 
launch, the Company has secured 
customer commitments, finalised 
land parcels, and progressed 
partnering agreements. TCS is 
engaging hyperscalers, semiconductor 
companies, and model providers 
while it also serves as the integration 
partner across infrastructure, 
engineering, and AI-led services.
To help clients accelerate their 
transformation journeys, TCS has created 
an AI Acceleration playbook ‘Innovate–
Build–Scale with AI’ to help clients move 
from isolated to enterprise-wide scaled 
AI deployments.
Innovate with AI – AI Immersion sessions 
bring together business and technology 
teams together to gain AI-fluency and 
identify high-impact business problems 
best suited for AI-led solutions, with a 
clear proof-to-value approach.
Build with AI – Accelerated delivery 
of outcomes with Rapid Build squads 
(Forward-Deployment Engineers) 
who solve high impact business 
problems with AI-first mindset and 
deliver production-ready solutions 
within 12–16 weeks. 
Scale with AI – Scaling AI within an 
enterprise requires a platform approach 
with strong focus on safety and security. 
TCS is working with its clients to deploy 
AI platforms and AI labs for scaled 
AI adoption. Supported by strong 
AI governance capabilities, TCS also 
helps clients implement the necessary 
guardrails to ensure responsible and 
secure AI adoption.
TCS has strengthened advisory and 
consulting capabilities across key growth 
areas such as cybersecurity, cloud, and 
enterprise platforms. Today, over 50% of 
experienced hires bring next-generation 
skills, positioning TCS to lead confidently 
into its AI-driven future.
This talent strategy is further supported 
by AI-enabled hiring, curated talent 
marketplaces and partnerships with 181 
academic institutions, helping TCS attract

complemented by flagship initiatives such 
as CodeVita
TM and HackQuest.

for TCS to make AI real for its clients. As organisations pursue higher levels of

AI-led transformation at TCS
AI with Purpose  
India AI Impact Summit 2026
Beyond enterprise transformation, TCS remained committed to societal progress. 
At the India AI Impact Summit 2026, TCS showcased its unique capability to scale AI 
responsibly, from foundational infrastructure to real-world, societal impact. Through 
live programs, hands-on immersions, and large-scale participation, TCS demonstrated 
its commitment to making AI accessible, human-centered, and inclusive at  a 
population scale. This effort reflects TCS’ belief that AI leadership is defined not just by 
technological depth, but by who it empowers and how effectively it transforms lives.
At the India AI Impact Summit 2026, 
the Tata AI Sakhi Immersion Programme 
brought the Tata Group’s vision of 
making AI a force for inclusion to life. 
The programme’s impact was immediate 
and measurable: in just 2.5 hours, 1,553 
women successfully completed 4,727 
AI-powered tasks.
The programme followed an immersive, 
hands-on format. Participants, or ‘Sakhis’, 
from rural India were organised into 
structured cohorts based on their digital 
proficiency and supported by a high-touch 
mentorship framework, with one mentor 
assigned for every five women. Using 
their own mobile phones and in their local 
languages, the Sakhis explored practical, 
real-world AI applications—from design 
ideation and marketing content creation 
to accessing government schemes and 
drafting business communications. The 
results were significant, with advanced 
cohorts achieved a 98% task completion 
rate, demonstrating high engagement 
and rapid development of capability 
and confidence. 
What truly set the programme apart 
was its focus on experiential learning, 
empowering women from rural India to 
confidently use AI as a practical tool for 
economic independence and self-reliance. 
The initiative successfully transformed 
AI from an abstract concept to a tangible 
tool, enabling women to integrate 
it meaningfully into their daily lives 
and livelihoods. 
Building on this strong foundation, the 
Tata AI Sakhi initiative is set to scale 
through broader regional outreach, 
expanded mentorship networks, and 
deeper ecosystem partnerships, with the 
goal of empowering thousands of women 
as AI-enabled entrepreneurs and agents of 
change across India.
When technology speaks the language of people and addresses their real 
needs, it becomes a tool of dignity and empowerment rather than exclusion.
Smriti Irani
Chairperson, Alliance for Global Good, Gender Equity & Equality, CII
At the India AI Impact Summit 2026, TCS 
conducted one of India’s largest single-
session AI training initiatives, upskilling 
over 2,000 students. The Tata 
Bharat YUVAi Hackathon was conceived 
with a clear vision: to democratise 
access to artificial intelligence and 
enable students from non engineering 
backgrounds to identify real problems in 
their own fields and build working digital 
solutions using AI tools in their own 
mother tongue  without any prior coding 
experience. The initiative proved that 
domain expertise, curiosity, and access 
to AI in native languages are sufficient to 
create meaningful AI-led solutions. 
The programme operated through 
a distributed format, with satellite 
hackathons conducted over six weeks 
across 22 colleges in 10 states, engaging 
more than 10,000 students ahead 
of the India AI Impact Summit 2026. 
Participants used voice-first, multilingual 
AI tools available in nine Indian 
languages, progressing from problem 
identification to working prototypes within 
90–120 minutes.
What set YUVAi apart was its strong focus 
on inclusivity. By removing barriers related 
to coding knowledge, English proficiency 
and prior technical exposure, the initiative 
enabled broad-based participation 
while delivering consistent outcomes at 
national scale. The programme created 
thousands of first-time AI builders, 
validated a multilingual operating 
framework and established a growing 
ecosystem of mentors.
The success at the summit laid 
the foundation for scaling YUVAi 
into a sustained, pan India talent 
development platform. 
I have come here today to 
feel the energy that you 
all have brought with you. 
The way you all are using 
technology to create new 
solutions, that’s phenomenal. 
What this proves is that AI 
can be used by everyone 
for solving your day-to-
day problems, for creating 
solutions that you need, and 
you understand. 
Ashwini Vaishnaw 
Honourable Minister of Railways, 
Information and Broadcasting, and 
Electronics and Information Technology

 AI with Purpose
Lloyds Banking Group, one of the UK’s 
largest financial services institutions, is on a 
mission to reimagine banking by embedding 
AI across every aspect of the enterprise. With 
a strong focus on delivering personalised, 
efficient, and secure banking experiences, 
the Group is scaling AI to transform 
customer engagement, product innovation, 
engineering productivity, colleague support, 
and core operations.
To accelerate this journey and move from 
experimentation to enterprise-wide impact, 
Lloyds Banking Group partnered with TCS.
As Generative AI emerged as a transformative 
technology, Lloyds Banking Group recognised 
the opportunity to unlock significant value—
but also the complexity of scaling it across a 
large, regulated organisation.
The bank needed to move beyond siloed 
AI initiatives to enterprise-wide adoption, 
enable self service innovation, establish 
robust guardrails, accelerate the journey 
With its extensive AI & Data expertise and 
its deep contextual knowledge of customer 
landscape, Lloyds Banking Group partnered 
with TCS in establishing a GenAI office to 
drive enterprise-wide AI adoption, following 
a thorough assessment of bank’s business & 
technology stack to define the architecture 
& roadmap for GenAI implementation. 
This provides an environment for 
colleagues to self-serve GenAI products 
and models, enabling development 
from concept to production, supported 
by frameworks, and guardrails to 
ensure scalable, safe and cost-efficient 
development of GenAI products.  This 
has significantly helped the bank in not 
only scaling GenAI adoption, but also in 
decentralisation & democratisation of AI 
across the enterprise.
The selection of TCS as one of our GenAI 
partners was a strategic decision driven 
by their commitment to innovation. 
TCS demonstrated a strong willingness 
to drive progress and align with our 
vision for GenAI at scale. Their existing 
knowledge of LBG’s ways of working and 
GCP estate made them an ideal partner to 
hit the ground running. Our collaboration 
with TCS has been instrumental in the 
successful launch of the GenAI workbench.
Ranil Boteju 
Chief Data & Analytics Officer 
Lloyds Banking Group
We need talented people; we

transformation and AI. That is 
why we choose TCS.
Marjan Rintel 
CEO, KLM
TCS as a strategic partner of Air France 
KLM has helped modernise customer 
and employee journeys across mobile, 
web, social, and airport touchpoints. This 
resulted in reduced passenger wait times, 
improved disruption handling, boosting 
direct digital sales, and enhanced end-to-
end service experience.
TCS partnered with Air France-KLM 
in their transformation journey to 
modernise its airline digital foundation on 
cloud. TCS completed a large scale, zero 
disruption exit from legacy infrastructure, 
safely relocating more than 1,200 mission 
critical systems to modern & future ready 
hybrid infrastructure. 
This complex transition ensured 
uninterrupted airline operations while 
improving resilience, reducing energy 
consumption, and delivering long-term 
cost efficiencies.
Building on this foundation, TCS is 
modernizing its data landscape on Google 
cloud platform. This modernization 
programme is already providing early 
benefits of more than 20% performance 
improvement in business intelligence & 
insights through the usage of cloud native 
& AI-powered services.
Today, this foundation enables AI first 
service delivery and intelligent business 
solutions. With AI, Air France-KLM is 
bringing a positive impact on the day 
in a life of individuals: inspiration & 
self-service for customers; assistance to 
business users like crew, ground handlers, 
MRO engineers; and acceleration in 
digital product development to architects, 
developers, testers & analysts.

technologies and business needs evolve.

Reimagining the Aerospace Value 
Chain with AI
Telefónica Germany drives OSS transformation with a data 
driven autonomous network
TCS’s Future-Ready Skies vision 
is focused on reimagining the 
aerospace value chain - from 
accelerating product innovation 
to optimising digitally driven 
production, and enabling insight-
led decisions through AI across 
manufacturing, flight operations 
and ground systems. 
TCS helps enterprises leverage AI to 
deliver safer, more seamless, and 
personalised passenger experiences at 
scale. TCS platforms power predictive 
maintenance and resilient fleet 
operations, driving reliability, efficiency, 
and sustainability.
TCS is supporting breakthrough innovations such as hydrogen propulsion and accelerating 
the transition to next-generation low-emission aviation.
TCS is supporting leading global aerospace companies in their digital and AI-led 
transformation journeys
Airbus and TCS have forged a multi-year strategic partnership, for establishing 
a joint AI Innovation Lab in India. TCS is working on the scope of AI model 
development, initially focusing on areas such as Computer Vision (e.g. Quality 
Control, EHS and Damage Assessment) with plans to expand into other areas. 
Telefónica Germany is a leading 
telecommunications company in Germany.  
It is a major driver of the country’s 
digitalisation efforts, with a strong focus 
on network expansion, superior customer 
experience, and continuous digital 
transformation to enable future growth. 
The company’s network transported 
6.4 billion GB of mobile data in 2025, 
surpassing competitors in the market. 
It is widely recognized for delivering an 
excellent customer experience powered by 
data driven decision-making and advanced 
digital capabilities.
The organisation was faced with the 
increasing challenge of managing 
rapidly growing data volumes across a 
heterogeneous and historically evolved 
data platform in operations landscape. 
Multiple tools and systems had been 
developed over time to address specific 
requirements, leading to higher complexity 
in data management, governance, and 
end-to-end transparency. At the same 
time, strengthening automation, analytics, 
and AI capabilities became a strategic 
priority to further improve operational 
efficiency, scalability, and resilience, while 
laying the foundation for more predictive 
and proactive operations. The company 
aimed to modernise parts of its application 
landscape. This included addressing legacy 
architectures, improving observability 
across next-generation operations, and 
enabling faster implementation of new 
data-driven use cases in a highly dynamic 
market environment.
TCS implemented a unified, cloud native 
data platform enabling self service data 
products based on a common data model, 
strong governance, and configurable 
data quality. The solution integrated data 
catalogs, automated data quality rules, and 
ticketing to create trusted data foundations. 
TCS also deployed a next generation AI/
ML and automation platform delivering 
TCS has signed a multi-year strategic partnership deal with GE Aerospace to optimise 
operational costs and enable future growth and scale. Through this strategic 
partnership, TCS will manage the majority of GE Aerospace enterprise application 
development, maintenance, rationalization, and standardization. TCS will leverage 
advanced software engineering practices, combined with AI and Generative AI, to 
drive faster time-to-value realisation, operational resilience, and productivity. 
AI driven analytics, actionable insights, 
and enhanced observability across IT and 
network operations, enabling predictive 
intelligence, anomaly detection, and 
closed loop automation. In parallel, legacy 
applications were modernised through 
consolidation, decommissioning, open 
source adoption, and migration to modern 
architectures. 
• ~30% cost reduction in application 
operations; 7 data platforms 
consolidated in unified data 
platform and governance
• 3 AI-driven critical network and 
data use cases live, including 
enabling 7% energy cost reduction.
• Automatization platform enables 
2X faster use case implementation; 
29 Operations & 10 Autonomous 
network-related use cases live.

Reimagining Public Services at Scale
TCS has played a pivotal technology role 
in advancing Ayushman Bharat Pradhan 
Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY 
2.0) and the National Health Claims 
Exchange (NHCX), driving large-scale 
digital transformation across India’s 
healthcare ecosystem.
TCS has modernized key PM-JAY 2.0 
systems, including hospital empanelment, 
transaction management, and claims 
processing, creating a scalable, 
interoperable platform that enables 
integration with multiple government 
health schemes.
With the rollout of NHCX, TCS-supported 
systems are shifting health claims 
processing from siloed workflows to 
an interoperable, standards-based 
ecosystem. As the national backbone for 
health claims exchange, NHCX enables 
real-time, transparent, and efficient 
data sharing between providers and 
payers across India. TCS has helped build 
and operationalize these integrations, 
allowing hospital systems (HMIS), payer 
platforms, and national digital health 
infrastructure to work together without 
requiring fundamental changes to existing 
provider systems.
Today, TCS-enabled PMJAY 2.0 and NHCX 
platforms are operating at scale across 
India, serving millions of beneficiaries 
and thousands of healthcare providers. 
These systems are accelerating claim 
settlements, improving transparency, 
reducing fraud, and enhancing the citizen 
experience—advancing India toward a 
digitally integrated, AI-ready, and citizen-
centric health insurance ecosystem.
Transforming Healthcare 
Services in India
Serviced by Software: An AI-led operating model for BFSI 
platforms
TCS BFSI Products & Platforms is a 
leading solutions provider for the 
financial services industry.
TCS designs, builds, operates, and 
continuously modernises these services to 
meet changing customer expectations and 
rapid technology shifts.
Over the past 18 months, TCS has 
embedded AI across the service value 
chain to create a next-generation ‘serviced 
by software’ model— now supporting 
more than 25 million customers. The 
platform uses over 100 AI agents 
across contact centres, back-office 
operations, customer communications, 
and complaints management, enabling 
capabilities such as speech recognition, 
call summarisation, complaint prediction, 
resolution-letter drafting, intelligent 
email and secure-message handling, and 
personalised customer journeys.
In the UK, TCS supports more than 35 
million life and pension policyholders, 
including through Diligenta, TCS’s wholly 
owned, FCA-regulated subsidiary. 
Together, TCS and Diligenta deliver 
BPaaS for leading life and pension 
providers including Standard Life, Aviva, 
Lloyds Banking Group, M&G, Nest, 
and NOW: Pensions.
TCS’ end-to-end servicing platform 
combines TCS BaNCS for Insurance, 
Intelligent Experience (IEX), and Quartz 
to deliver policy administration, customer 
service, and digital transformation. 
This model has delivered sustained, 
measurable impact. The AI-led contact 
centre has reduced after-call work by 
40% and cut call quality assessment and 
audit effort by 80%, while improving data 
integrity and removing human bias from 
call analysis and scoring. Early-warning 
and complaints-propensity models have 
driven proactive intervention, contributing 
to a 10% reduction in complaints and 
lower rework. AI-assisted complaint 
response generation has also reduced 
turnaround times from hours to minutes.
Collectively, these capabilities have 
increased service speed for policyholders 
and intermediaries while creating a more 
scalable, cost-effective operating model.

The Passport Seva Programme is a global 
benchmark in e-governance delivered 
through a public-private partnership. In 
2025-26, TCS successfully rolled out the 
PSP 2.0 application across 37 Regional 
Passport Offices and 200 missions. It 
is a future-ready, resilient, automated, 
and intelligent system refresh with 
improved reliability that enables the 
issuance of e-Passports to Indian citizens 
worldwide. Each e-Passport contains 
an embedded RFID chip and antenna 
storing the holder’s demographic and 
biometric data. The chip is powered by 
the reader’s electromagnetic field and 
does not require a battery. The e-passport 
rollout is expected to deter identity theft, 
forgery, and enhance connectivity for a 
streamlined immigration process.

data-driven retailer supported by globally best-in-class modern

provide the right base for long-term growth, and create superior 
customer experience.

building operations from traditional automation to enterprise 
autonomy by combining their expertise in IT , cloud, operational 
technology, and AI analytics for greater efficiency.
Collaborated with AMD to help enterprises scale AI adoption from 
pilots to production, modernise legacy environments, and build 
secure, high performance digital workplaces. 
Signed a multi-year partnership with ServiceNow for developing 
trusted, AI powdered solutions on the ServiceNow platform to 
reimagine back office functions such as HR, finance, supply chain, 
procurement, and employee services.
Partnered with OpenAI to drive AI-powered innovation across 
enterprise, consumer, and social sectors. This partnership 
spans multiple high-impact areas, including powering AI-led 
innovation across Tata Group companies, jointly accelerating 
AI transformation across industries globally, and establishing AI 
infrastructure with an initial 100 MW capacity, with an option to 
scale to 1 GW . This infrastructure will power next-generation AI 
workloads and position India as a global AI hub. 
Launched Rapid Outcome AI Platform, built on NVIDIA, helping 
enterprises accelerate their journey from AI experimentation to 
scalable, real-world business outcomes.
Inaugurated Gemini Experience Center (GEC) at TCS’ Innovation 
Hub in Troy, Michigan, enabling manufacturers to co-innovate 
and scale cutting-edge Physical AI solutions for smarter, resilient 
operations. The centre forms part of the global expansion of TCS’ 
GEC network, which now includes centres in Bangalore, New York, 
Chennai, Riyadh, Singapore and São Paulo.
TCS strengthened its strategic collaboration with ABB across 
IT, AI and engineering services. The Company also extended 
its 18-year partnership to implement AI-driven IT operations 
globally for ABB, headquartered in Switzerland.
TCS and Cisco launched a Center of Excellence in Hyderabad for 
Autonomous Enterprise Operations. The initiative is designed 
to help enterprises transition from rule-based automation to 
intelligent, self-governing operations capable of understanding 
real-time context and taking autonomous actions.
At the India AI Impact Summit, TCS and the Tata Group 
showcased a full-stack AI story - from ‘Infrastructure to 
Intelligence’- anchored by a large-scale AI Pavilion that 
engaged a wide audience both on-ground and digitally. 
Together, they also advanced AI adoption and inclusion 
through practical AI masterclasses across four tracks, 
including robotics, financial services, and public services.
As a longstanding strategic partner to the World Economic 
Forum, TCS had a significant presence at their annual 
meeting in Davos, Switzerland. This included the flagship 
TCS reception attended by world leaders, CXO roundtables 
in partnership with academia partners MIT and CMU on 
advancing the strategic deployment of AI in enterprises, 
a ‘Future Leaders’ session in partnership with Pearson 
and a roundtable for CEOs of the Semiconductor and AI 
ecosystem. TCS demonstrated a Generative AI showcase 
at its Tata Tea stall at the event, with an AI Avatar flavorist 
who helped people determine which type of tea was best 
suited for them. During the event, the Chairman of the 
Tata Group and the Chief Minister of Maharashtra also 
jointly announced a new ‘Innovation City’ in Mumbai and a 
strategic partnership to develop and implement a circular 
economy plan for making the city more sustainable, driven 
by an AI-first approach.
Established a collaboration with GitLab Inc., the intelligent 
orchestration platform for DevSecOps, to combine TCS’ 
expertise in AI-led enterprise transformation capabilities with 
GitLab’s pre-built AI agents and intelligent orchestration for 
software development. 
Expanded strategic collaboration with Zscaler to deliver 
secure, AI-driven digital workplace experiences for the 
modern enterprise.

Revenue Trend (H crore)
In FY 2026, TCS achieved a year-over year revenue growth of 4.6%, led 
by focused and effective execution.
On a constant currency basis, revenue declined by 2.4%. The decline 
was largely a result of one of the Company’s large transformation 
programmes in India coming to an end this year .
Over the past five financial years, the company recorded a compound 
annual growth rate (CAGR) of 10.2%, highlighting the resilience and 
scalability of its business model.

In FY 2026, TCS reported an operating margin of 25.0%, an improvement of 70 
basis points compared to FY 2025, and was at a 4-year high.
Improvement of business mix, productivity and realisation, rebalancing of 
pyramid along with favourable currency movements helped the expansion 
of margins.
These were offset by investments in talent and capability building, 
and other investments for strengthening ecosystem partnerships and 
increasing Go-to-Market pipeline.

TCS remains firmly committed to shareholders through a consistent and 
shareholder friendly dividend policy, while prudently expanding investments 
under the ‘Build-Partner-Acquire’ framework to strengthen long-term growth. 
Based on the company’s performance, the Board of Directors have 
declared three interim dividends of ₹11 each, a special dividend of ₹46, and

this AGM), for a total of ₹110 per share for FY 2026. TCS has consistently 
declared dividend every quarter since its listing, complemented by three 
bonus issues and five buyback offers.

Ignite My Future: Empowering Communities

Employment
TCS Ignite My Future (IMF) is a 
transdisciplinary education programme 
that ignites the spark of curiosity and 
problem solving through Computational 
Thinking (CT), a foundational 21
st century 
skill for successful careers in every sector.
Since its inception in 2017,  
IMF has enhanced the lives of over  
2.7 million teachers and students across 
17 countries.
In FY 2026, IMF reached 1,978 educators 
and 83,807 students.
Equipping students with the skills, 
confidence and mindset necessary to 
pursue careers of the future with TCS go 
Innovate Together (goIT)
TCS go Innovate Together (goIT) is a 
no-cost digital innovation and career 
readiness programme designed to equip 
students from diverse backgrounds with 
future-ready skills. It encourages them to 
become innovators and address real-world 
societal challenges.
Since its launch in 2009, goIT has 
positively impacted 
396,342 students in 
its growing presence across 67 countries.
In FY 2026, goIT empowered 49,070 
students and educators around the world.
Youth Employment Programme Loreto College

TCS goIT students New York

of thinking, a way of contributing. 
Our students didn’t just learn how 
to solve problems; they learned 
what it means to be responsible 
citizens. Supported by the TCS IMF 
team, this programme showed 
how education rooted in real-world 
relevance can empower students to 
become innovative problem solvers 
in their communities.

to students immediately and,

Education
TCS Youth Employment Programme 
(YEP) addresses youth unemployment 
by upskilling students from marginalised 
communities, equipping them with 
industry relevant skills, and facilitating 
placement opportunities. It bridges 
the gap between the academic and 
professional world while enabling socio 
economic mobility.
TCS Women Empowerment  
Programme (WEP) focuses on providing 
access to essential services in the 
hardest-to-reach rural locations in India 
by creating digital entrepreneurs within 
marginalised communities.
Since its inception in 2014, WEP has 
created 
1,866 entrepreneurs of which 
1,533 are active, comprising 87% women 
and 52% from marginalised communities, 
serving 8,371 villages across 42 
districts by offering essential services 
like document generation, government 
scheme enrolment, online form filling, and 
banking transactions, among others.

 Social Capital
Conservation and 
restoration of 
traditional water 
systems across India
Turning scars into 
strength 
Rajon ki Baoli, built in 1506 during the 
Lodi era, is a four-level stepwell situated 
within the Mehrauli Archaeological Park. 
Once a vital water source, its revival called 
for more than conservation - it demanded 
systemic restoration.
A 2023 Indian Council of Medical Research 
(ICMR) multi-centre study found that 11% 
of rural households reported burn injury 
patients compared to 5% in urban areas³, 
showing how access to immediate medical 
care remains uneven.
The TCS Foundation supported an 
organisation, founded by a burn 
survivor. This organisation offers 
holistic rehabilitation, which includes 
reconstructive surgeries, awareness 
and counselling to help survivors regain 
confidence and reintegrate into society. 
TCS Foundation provided financial 
assistance for free surgeries and post-
surgery rehabilitation of burn survivors.
Every year, millions of Indians suffer 
burn injuries, most of them preventable. 
Behind these numbers are families who 
lose not only health but also livelihoods, 
education, and identity.
According to the World Health 
Organisation, India records nearly 70 lakh 
burn injuries annually, with over 1.4 lakh 
deaths each year ¹. That is one life lost 
every four minutes. What makes it worse 
is that four out of every five burn victims 
are women or children², and most cases 
occur in low-income or rural households.
To prevent groundwater contamination, 
TCS Foundation collaborated for 
restoration and rejuvenation of Rajon ki 
Baoli. Overflow from the local Sewage 
Treatment Plant (STP) was redirected, 
stormwater networks were repaired, and 
nearby settlements were connected to 
the sewerage grid.
The front plaza was regraded and paved 
with grass-jointed stone over a sand bed; 
a simple, sustainable intervention to 
reduce sedimentation into the baoli.
A three-pronged approach was 
adopted to improve water quality:

surgeries were assisted in FY 2026 and

technology, and cybersecurity, and

Established with the support of the TCS 
Foundation and operationally managed 
by the institute, the Centre of Excellence 
is envisioned as a future-ready hub for 
advanced learning, applied research, and 
innovation. Bringing together emerging 
technologies such as artificial intelligence, 
drone technology, and more, the Centre 
focuses on hands-on learning through 
modular laboratories, real-world projects, 
and applied problem-solving. The CoE 
aims to incubate 100 startups. 
TCS Foundation supported a project to 
launch a Centre of Excellence (CoE) in 
Gorakhpur, Uttar Pradesh. The CoE aims 
to nurture and empower talent from 
Eastern Uttar Pradesh (Purvanchal) in 
emerging technologies such as artificial 
intelligence (AI), drone technology, 3D 
printing (additive manufacturing), space 
The aim is to create a network of schools, 
teachers, and after-school centres by 
creating a learning infrastructure and 
build a network of teacher training 
university and online certification 
programmes. The programme is 
a blended teacher training course 
that prepares educators to equip 
students for the 21
st century by using 
incubated schools as practical training 
environments. The programme was built 
to supply the system with a teaching 
and coaching workforce that is better 
prepared to reinvent education. The 
programme runs two tracks - one for 
teachers and one for coaches - tailored 
to strengthen instructional practice and 
coaching leadership.
 Story 1  A first-year teacher, part of 
the teacher track in this programme 
who through the programmes’ Virtual 
Elective session, her first experience 
with online learning, participated in 
electives on Whole Child Development 
and Building Vocabulary in the 
foundational years. She found the 
format flexible and practical, enabling 
immediate classroom application, and 
gained a holistic approach to lesson 
planning by integrating cognitive, 
language, physical, and social-
emotional development, an experience 
she described as rich and impactful.
 Story 2  It takes a village to raise a child, 
a phrase that is often heard. The founders 
of a community-based school translated 
this idea into everyday practice. Their 
community board is one of the most deeply 
involved - not just in decision-making, but 
in the lives of each child. They actively 
discuss every student’s circumstances, often 
visiting homes and stepping in with support 
wherever it is needed.
With just four local teachers, a single 
school campus in the entire village, and 
a committed community, this school is 
redefining what community-based learning 
can look like - especially in one of the most 
conflict-affected regions of the country. 
The CoE has been set up to support 
the skilling and innovation needs 
of Eastern UP , where access to 
advanced technological infrastructure 
and sustained industry-academia 
collaboration is still emerging. By 
creating a centralised platform focused 
on selected high-impact technology 
areas, the CoE aims to strengthen 
regional research and innovation efforts, 
support entrepreneurship, and enhance 
employability, while contributing to 
broader regional priorities and national 
development objectives.

Natural  Capital
TCS recognises environmental protection as essential to long-term value creation, 
reflecting the Tata Group’s commitment to environmental stewardship, embodied in 
Project Aalingana. TCS focuses on minimising environmental impacts by embracing 
Aalingana’s interlinked pillars: driving the decarbonisation of its businesses and value 
chain; applying a systemic, circular economy approach to reduce resource use and 
waste; and preserving and restoring the natural environment. TCS’ Natural Capital 
approach emphasises efficient use of resources, protection of ecosystems, and 
integration of environmental considerations into operational decision-making.

Fauna
Water Management 
TCS focuses on reducing freshwater withdrawal through recycle 
and reuse initiatives, sewage treatment, enhancing water-use 
efficiency, and rainwater harvesting. Special emphasis is placed 
on managing water risks in water-stressed locations, supported by 
governance mechanisms, monitoring and employee engagement. 
Green building design promotes sustainable water practices 
including water recharge across few of the Company campuses. 
All new campuses have been designed for higher water efficiency, 
rainwater harvesting and treatment and recycling of sewage.
Waste Management
TCS focuses on waste reduction at source, segregation, recycling, and 
safe disposal across its operations. TCS is committed to the circular 
economy principles, including minimisation of waste disposed to 
landfill, responsible management of e-waste, battery waste and 
hazardous waste by engagement with authorised recyclers and 
resellers for appropriate recovery/reuse. TCS is also committed to 
advancing zero waste to landfill practices across its operations. 9 TCS 
locations are already certified for ‘Zero Waste to Landfill’ with 99*% 
of waste diverted away from landfill and more locations are planned.
Biodiversity
Tata Group’s Project Aalingana emphasises the need to manage company’s  impacts 
and dependencies on biodiversity and enhance their performance on biodiversity 
conservation. TCS Nature and Biodiversity policy outlines TCS’ commitment and plan of 
action to conserve, preserve and enhance nature and biodiversity.
During the year, the Company has conducted biodiversity assessment of campuses and 
raised employee awareness through sessions, webinars and nature walks/ trails. TCS’ flora 
and fauna conservation initiatives at campus level include:

Shareholder Connect
Initiatives
Key Actions for Shareholders
The Company remains committed to delivering shareholder-centric solutions that address specific requirements through the adoption 
of technology-driven initiatives, strengthening shareholder engagement and enhancing awareness. A dedicated investor services 
team promptly addresses shareholder queries and facilitates constructive engagement, promoting transparency, trust, and long-term 
relationships. These efforts reinforce the Company’s commitment to ensuring that shareholders remain well-informed, valued, and 
integral to its sustained growth and success. Key initiatives and other relevant information are outlined below:
	 The Company has developed eTDS Portal for shareholders, providing a secure self-service view 
of their consolidated dividend and tax information. The Portal offers financial year wise and 
quarter-wise details of dividend income, including particulars of Tax Deducted at Source (TDS), 
shareholding in TCS across all demat accounts and/or physical folios and facility for downloading TDS 
certificates. Link to access the portal: https://on.tcs.com/eTDS-portal.
	 Web-based query resolution systems:
	 	 Swayam is an application to view records, download documents, raise queries etc. 
Link to access the application: https://swayam.in.mpms.mufg.com.
	 iDIA is a chatbot which provides quick guidance on queries raised or directs shareholders to 
appropriate channel to resolve their queries. 
Link to the chatbot: https://in.mpms.mufg.com.
	 Voluntary reminder letters and SMS alerts are sent to claim unclaimed dividends before its statutory 
transfer to the Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF) Authority. Details of unclaimed dividends 
are available at https://on.tcs.com/TCS-IEPF.
	 A special cycle of remittance was conducted twice during the year to remit unclaimed dividends directly 
into the updated bank account of shareholders before transfer of such dividends to IEPF. 
	 KYC letters are sent to encourage shareholders to update their KYC details and dematerialize their  
shares held in physical form.
	 Personalised TDS calculations on dividend are provided in the e-credit intimations sent to shareholders.
	 Quarterly financial results are sent to shareholders at their registered email address.
	 Periodic updates through earnings calls, press conferences, press releases and other investor 
communications are provided under the ‘Investors’ section of the Company’s website.
	 Investor FAQs covering aspects such as unclaimed dividend, IEPF , KYC updation, taxation of dividend 
distribution, opening of a special window for lodgement of share transfer requests and DigiLocker facility 
etc., are made available at https://on.tcs.com/Investor-FAQs. 
   Mandatory KYC Updation
Shareholders are requested to update KYC details in order to receive timely payment of dividend(s) and avoid 
any withholding of dividend(s). For detailed procedure refer note no. 11 of the AGM Notice.
   Dematerialisation of shares
As per SEBI mandate, requests for transfer, transmission and transposition of securities, are processed only in 
dematerialised form. Accordingly, Shareholders are encouraged to dematerialize their shares held in physical 
form to ensure faster, safer and more efficient services. Shareholders may contact the Company/RTA for 
dematerialisation of such shares.

4. Company’s performance and state of affairs
 On a consolidated basis, the revenue from operations for 
FY 2026 was ₹2,67,021 crore, higher by 4.6% over the 
previous year’s revenue from operations of ₹2,55,324 crore.  
The profit for the year attributable to shareholders 
(excluding exceptional items) for FY 2026 was ₹52,820 crore, 
registering a growth of 8.8% over the profit for the year 
attributable to shareholders of ₹48,553 crore in FY 2025.
 On a standalone basis, the revenue from operations for 
FY 2026 was ₹2,20,938 crore, higher by 2.8% over the 
previous year’s revenue from operations of ₹2,14,853 crore.  
The profit for the year attributable to shareholders (excluding  
exceptional items) in FY 2026 was ₹52,391 crore, registering 
a growth of 9.0% over the profit for the year attributable to 
shareholders of ₹48,057 crore in FY 2025.
 The Company did not undergo any change in the nature of its 
business during FY 2026.
 There have been no material changes and commitments, 
affecting the financial position of the Company, that have 
occurred between the end of the financial year to which the 
financial statements relate and the date of this Report.

 Key developments during the year under review:
 ListEngage Midco, LLC & ListEngage, LLC
 On October 10, 2025, an Equity Purchase Agreement was 
executed between the Company, ListEngage Midco, LLC and 
ListEngage Holdings, LLC for acquisition of 100% ownership 
interest in ListEngage Midco, LLC, incorporated in the State of 
Delaware, USA, along with its subsidiary ListEngage, LLC, for 
a consideration of US$69 million (₹612 crore). This acquisition 
positions the Company to capitalize on ListEngage’s strong 
Salesforce ecosystem presence, including advisory board 
participation across Marketing Cloud, Data Cloud and 
Agentforce, as well as its close alignment with Salesforce’s 
sales teams. ListEngage leverages the Company’s expansive 
customer base to accelerate growth.
 Coastal Cloud
 On December 10, 2025, the Company executed Securities 
Purchase Agreement and Plan of Merger (“Agreement”) 
for acquisition of 100% ownership interest in Coastal 
Cloud Holdings, LLC (“Coastal Cloud”) in the USA with its 
subsidiaries, through ListEngage Midco, LLC (“ListEngage 
Midco”), a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company.
 Subsequently, on December 15, 2025, ListEngage Midco 
incorporated two wholly owned subsidiaries in the USA  
viz. TCS North America Corporation and Trident LE LLC, to 
consummate the aforesaid acquisition.
 On January 14, 2026, ListEngage Midco acquired 86% 
ownership interest in Coastal Cloud through merger of 
Trident LE LLC with Coastal Cloud and remaining 14% 
through acquisition of SCP V-B Blocker III LLC (“SCP Blocker”) 
via TCS North America Corporation, for a consideration of 
US$707 million (₹6,386 crore). The name of SCP Blocker was 
changed to Coastal Cloud NA LLC in February 2026.
 The acquisition of ListEngage and Coastal Cloud would 
significantly strengthen the Company’s global salesforce 
aspirations by bringing together comprehensive, multi-cloud 
Salesforce expertise across industries globally with enhanced 
talent and complementary delivery capabilities. The Company 
is now better equipped to deliver stronger client outcomes 
and accelerate growth across all key global markets.
 HyperVault AI Data Center Limited
 HyperVault AI Data Center Limited (“HyperVault”) was 
incorporated as a wholly owned subsidiary on October 29, 
2025 in India. Subsequently, on November 20, 2025, the 
Company entered into a Securities Subscription Agreement 
and a Shareholders’ Agreement (“Transaction Documents”) 
with TPG Terabyte Bidco Pte. Ltd. (“TPG”) and HyperVault 
for an investment by the Company and TPG in HyperVault 
up to ₹18,000 crore over the next few years, in the ratio of 
51:49 respectively.
 Upon satisfaction of all conditions precedent under the 
Transaction Documents (as amended), TPG subscribed to 
49% of the total paid-up share capital amounting to  
₹199.4 crore on a diluted basis, of HyperVault on  
March 9, 2026. Consequently, HyperVault ceased to be  
a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company.
 Through this partnership, the Company seeks to support 
HyperVault’s Gigawatt-scale AI-ready infrastructure build 
with a plan to create AI-ready data centres, having capacity 
in excess of a Gigawatt over the next few years. HyperVault 
aims to facilitate AI-led innovation while aligning its operations 
with the principles of sustainability, governance and 
long-term value creation. This aligns with the Company’s 
aspiration of becoming world’s largest AI-led technology 
services company.

6. Directors’ Responsibility Statement
 Based on the framework of internal financial controls and 
compliance systems established and maintained by the 
Company, the work performed by the internal, statutory and 
secretarial auditors and external consultants, including the 
audit of internal financial controls over financial reporting by 
the statutory auditors and the reviews performed by  
the management and the relevant Board Committees, 
including the Audit Committee, the Board is of the opinion 
that the Company’s internal financial controls were 
adequate and effective during FY 2026. Pursuant to Section 
134(5) of the Act, the Board of Directors, to the best of its 
knowledge and ability, confirm that: 
 i. In the preparation of the annual accounts, the 
applicable accounting standards have been followed 
and there are no material departures;
 ii. They have selected such accounting policies and 
applied them consistently and made judgements and 
estimates that are reasonable and prudent so as to 
give a true and fair view of the state of affairs of the 
Company at the end of the financial year and of the 
profit of the Company for that period;
 iii. They have taken proper and sufficient care for 
the maintenance of adequate accounting records 
in accordance with the provisions of the Act for 
safeguarding the assets of the Company and for 
preventing and detecting fraud and other irregularities;
 iv. They have prepared the annual accounts on a 
going concern basis;
 v. They have laid down internal financial controls to be 
followed by the Company and such internal financial 
controls are adequate and operating effectively;
 vi. They have devised proper systems to ensure 
compliance with the provisions of all applicable 
laws and that such systems are adequate and 
operating effectively.

10. Board evaluation 1
 The Board of Directors has carried out an annual evaluation 
of its own performance, board committees and individual 
directors pursuant to the provisions of the Act and SEBI 
Listing Regulations. The criteria is broadly based on the 
Guidance Note on Board Evaluation issued by the SEBI.
 The performance of the Board was evaluated by the Board 
after seeking inputs from all the Directors on the basis 
of criteria such as the board composition and structure, 
effectiveness of board processes, information and 
functioning, etc.
 The performance of the Committees was evaluated by the 
Board after seeking inputs from the Committee Members on 
the basis of criteria such as the composition of committees, 
effectiveness of committee meetings, etc.
 In a separate meeting of Independent Directors, performance 
of Non-Independent Directors, the Board as a whole and 
Chairman of the Company was evaluated, taking into account 
the views of Executive and Non-Executive Directors.
 The Board and the Nomination and Remuneration 
Committee (“NRC”) reviewed the performance of individual 
directors on the basis of criteria such as contribution of the 
individual director to the Board and Committee meetings 
like preparedness on the issues to be discussed, meaningful 
and constructive contribution and inputs in meetings, etc.
 At the Board meeting that followed the meeting of 
the Independent Directors and meeting of NRC, the 
performance of the Board, its Committees and individual 
directors was also discussed. Performance evaluation of 
Independent Directors was done by the entire Board.

26. Disclosures under the Sexual Harassment of 
Women at Workplace (Prevention, Prohibition 
and Redressal) Act, 2013 [“POSH Act”]
 The Company follows a zero-tolerance approach towards 
sexual harassment and remains firmly committed to 
ensuring the safety, dignity and well-being of all employees. 
It strives to foster a safe, inclusive and respectful workplace 
across all its global operations.
 The Company has implemented a Global Policy on the 
Prevention of Sexual Harassment, aligned with the POSH 
Act and other applicable laws across the jurisdiction in 
which it operates. Internal Committees (“ICs”)  have been 
constituted in accordance with the requirements of the POSH 
Act. Multiple reporting channels are available for reporting 
concerns, including the Company intranet for TCS employees 
and a dedicated email address (ic.posh@tcs.com) for others.
 All complaints are addressed with due sensitivity, fairness 
and confidentiality, with appropriate safeguards to protect 
the privacy and reputation of all individuals involved. 
Based on the findings of the inquiry, suitable corrective 
& disciplinary actions including warning, apology, 
reassignment, separation or other remedial measures are 
taken as warranted.
 The Company continues to strengthen awareness and 
prevention through regular training of IC members, 
structured awareness programmes, induction sessions 
for new employees and ongoing e-learning modules for 
employees, trainees and associates. Approximately 97% 
of employees were covered through these initiatives in 
FY 2026. Regular communications, including emails and 
workplace collaterals are also used to reinforce the expected 
standards of professional conduct.
 The details of complaints received, disposed and pending, 
during FY 2026 are as follows:
